title: Reproducibility manifest
description: CONTRACTS HĐ-13. Acceptance criterion: hand this file to somebody else and they rebuild the same Decision Card, differing only in wall-clock time. Every field below exists because leaving it out breaks exactly that — including `bootstrap`, without which the confidence interval cannot be reproduced at all.

git_sha.description: The code that produced the card. Lower-case hex so a rebuilt manifest cannot differ by letter case alone.

docker_image_digest.description: Null when the run was not containerised. HĐ-7.4 requires the same image for every candidate in one comparison; recording it is how that is checkable afterwards.

anchor_config_version.description: Mandatory (HĐ-8.3 law 3): a recommendation computed under unknown anchors cannot be rebuilt.

bootstrap.description: Added at 2.2.0. The CI on the card comes from a random resample; without the seed two people running this manifest get two intervals, and that difference is not wall-clock time.

benchmark_host.description: HĐ-7.4: same machine, same allocation, same thread count for every candidate — otherwise even the relative comparison is meaningless. `cpu_affinity` and `logical_cores` record what the run actually got: G4 reads wall-clock latency, and the same candidate measured 59.30 ms pooled p99 unpinned against 16.10 ms pinned to two cores. Both are optional so manifests written before anyone looked stay valid — absent means not recorded, which is the honest reading.

cpu_affinity.description: Cores the process was confined to, as the OS reported during the run.

logical_cores.description: Cores the machine has, so cores_allocated reads as a share.

affinity_source.description: Where the mask came from. `script` means the run pinned itself, so re-running it reproduces the same protection; `inherited` means it took whatever it was launched with. A mask alone cannot tell the two apart.

created_at.description: ISO-8601. The one field a rebuild is allowed to differ on.

episode_contexts.description: The conditions themselves, not just their ids. episode_context_id is a hash (HĐ-3.1) and does not invert, so a manifest carrying only ids proves which episodes ran but leaves a rebuild unable to recompute their metrics — which is the acceptance test of this section.

sensor_noise.description: HĐ-2.5 amplitudes for this run. Required on the manifest because episode_context_id does not hash them: two runs at the same seeds under different sigma share every context id while being two experiments.
